# Threat coverage

<!-- Generated by scripts/coverage.js. Do not edit by hand; run `node scripts/coverage.js`. -->

This is the catalog of fake-interview and supply-chain techniques RepoCanary detects, and it is measured, not asserted. Every row below is produced by running the real detection engine over a synthetic corpus of the techniques these campaigns use (Contagious Interview, BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, and the wider npm and PyPI supply-chain playbook), and recording exactly which rules fire and what verdict results. Nothing here is run, cloned, or installed: each sample is scanned as text, the same path a real scan uses.

Regenerate with `node scripts/coverage.js`. CI runs `node scripts/coverage.js --check` so this file cannot drift from the rules.

## At a glance

- **101** distinct malicious techniques in the corpus, across **9** categories
- **100%** caught (each flagged for review or convicted outright)
- **94** distinct detection rules exercised by the corpus
- **6** evasion cases the tool honestly does not catch, held as runnable samples (listed at the end, not hidden). THREAT-MODEL.md argues the wider set of limits.

Verdict column: **RED** = do not run, a high-confidence signal fired; **flag** = flagged for human review; **green** = nothing known matched.

| `a7-native-build-at-install` | gypfile: true compiles and runs a native build during npm install | flag | `native-build-at-install (m)` |
| `a8-odd-dependency-mix` | a frontend app that also pulls in server and raw network packages | flag | `odd-dependency-mix (m)` |

## Documented evasions (known blind spots)

A tool that claims to catch everything is lying. These are techniques the static engine does not reliably catch, kept in the corpus so the limit is measured and visible rather than quietly forgotten. Green never means safe; it means nothing known matched.

| Technique | What it is | Verdict | Rules that fired |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `g17-workflow-remote-script` | a CI workflow pipes a script from an unknown host into a shell; it runs on the CI provider's machines, so it is reported as a note, not a caution | green | `workflow-remote-script (l)` |
| `z1-runtime-staging` | clean loader; payload only ever arrives from a normal-looking API at run time | green | (none) |
| `z2-clean-registry-dep` | malice would live in a dependency that resolves cleanly from the registry | green | (none) |
| `z3-social-only` | no malicious code committed; the attack is an instruction delivered elsewhere | green | (none) |
| `z5-uncorroborated-lookalike` | a one-edit lookalike in an established repository with no other signal stays informational | green | `typosquat-dependency (l)` |
| `z4-slopsquat-hallucinated-name` | a plausible but non-existent package name an LLM might hallucinate and an attacker register | green | (none) |
